back: The splitting of a heavy nucleus into two medium nuclei, with 2-3 neutrons and energy released.
The joining of two light nuclei into a heavier nucleus, releasing energy.
Products have higher binding energy per nucleon (nearer the peak at A ≈ 56), so mass decreases: ΔE = c²Δm.
Neutrons from one fission cause further fissions; steady when on average exactly one does.
Slows fast neutrons (water or graphite) so they cause fission more readily.
Absorb neutrons (boron or cadmium) to control the fission rate.
Very high temperature (to overcome electrostatic repulsion) and high density (frequent collisions).
Fission of U-235 about 200 MeV; D-T fusion 17.6 MeV, but more per nucleon.
